lead: Diabetes in pregnancy is either pre-existing (type 1 or 2), gestational (glucose intolerance first found in pregnancy, gone after birth; 85–90%), or overt diabetes first found in pregnancy at diabetic levels (treated as pre-existing). Good glucose control prevents most of its harm to mother and baby.
f: Risk factors for GDM

Strong (screen with OGTT): previous GDM, BMI over 30, previous macrosomic baby, first-degree relative with diabetes · Others: age 35 or more, PCOS, multiparity, previous unexplained stillbirth, steroids

sc: High glucose at 26 wk, normal 6 wk after birth → GDM
Fasting 7.8 at 10 wk → Overt diabetes: treat as pre-existing

f: Pathophysiology

From 20 wk placental hormones (hPL, cortisol) cause insulin resistance · Pedersen hypothesis: glucose crosses the placenta, insulin does not → fetal hyperinsulinaemia → macrosomia, RDS, neonatal hypoglycaemia · Anomalies need high glucose in weeks 3–8: pre-existing diabetes only, not GDM · Features: often none; candida, UTI, large for dates, polyhydramnios (fetal polyuria) · Glycosuria is a poor test (low renal threshold)
Screening and the 75 g OGTT

Previous GDM: OGTT at 16 wk; normal → repeat at 24–28 wk · Other risk factors: OGTT at 24–28 wk · Pre-existing: no OGTT; HbA1c at booking · Normal diet 3 days, overnight fast, 75 g glucose, 2 h sample · GDM: fasting ≥ 5.6 mmol/L (100 mg/dL) or 2 h ≥ 7.8 (140): any one value · Overt: fasting ≥ 7.0 (126) or 2 h ≥ 11.1 (200) · mg/dL ÷ 18 = mmol/L

sc: Glycosuria 1+, OGTT normal → Low renal threshold: normal
tr: The load is 75 g, not 75 mg; never diagnose from the urine dipstick

f: Investigations in pre-existing diabetes

HbA1c (aim under 6.5%), creatinine and urine protein, fundoscopy at booking and each trimester, FBC, MSU · Fetus: early dating scan, anomaly scan + fetal echocardiography at 18–20 wk, growth scans every 4 wk from 24–36 wk, CTG late
Maternal and fetal complications

Mother: hypoglycaemia, DKA, pre-eclampsia, polyhydramnios, preterm labour, infections, worse retinopathy and nephropathy; obstructed labour, operative birth, PPH · Type 2 diabetes in about 50% within 10 years after GDM · Fetus: miscarriage, anomalies (pre-existing only) · Commonest anomaly: cardiac; most characteristic: caudal regression · Macrosomia; FGR with vascular disease; unexplained stillbirth after 36 wk · Birth: shoulder dystocia, Erb palsy · Neonate: hypoglycaemia (commonest), RDS, polycythaemia, jaundice, hypocalcaemia

sc: Type 1 with nephropathy, small fetus → FGR (vascular disease)

f: Pre-pregnancy and antenatal care

HbA1c under 6.5% before conceiving; above 10%: avoid pregnancy for now · Folic acid 5 mg from 3 months before conception to 12 wk · Stop ACE inhibitors, ARBs, statins; oral drugs except metformin → insulin · MDT clinic, aspirin 75 mg from 12 wk, BP and urine every visit · Targets: fasting under 5.3, 1 h after meals under 7.8, 2 h under 6.4 mmol/L

sc: Type 2 on enalapril and atorvastatin, planning pregnancy → Stop both; folic acid 5 mg

f: Drugs

GDM ladder: diet → metformin (500 mg/day up to 2 g/day; first drug) → insulin · Glibenclamide 2.5–15 mg if no insulin (neonatal hypoglycaemia) · Soluble insulin before meals; isophane at bedtime for high fasting glucose · Type 1: about 0.7 U/kg/day early, 1 U/kg/day or more late; basal-bolus is best · Steroids and β-agonists raise insulin needs

sc: GDM, 2 wk of diet, fasting 5.9 → Add metformin
New GDM, fasting 7.4 at diagnosis → Insulin straight away

f: Timing and mode of birth
Pre-existing: 37⁺⁰–38⁺⁶ wk by induction (NICE); local units often 38–39 wk · GDM, controlled: 38 wk to 40⁺⁶ wk · EFW over 4.5 kg: offer elective caesarean (shoulder dystocia)
Labour and after birth

Glucose 4–7 mmol/L in labour; hourly checks; CTG; CS first on the list · Type 1: insulin + dextrose from established labour; never insulin without dextrose · Baby: feed within 30–60 min, then 2–3-hourly; heel-prick glucose from 2 h (aim over 2.6) · GDM: stop all drugs; fasting glucose or OGTT at 6 wk, then yearly · Type 1: return to the pre-pregnancy dose or lower (placenta gone)

sc: Type 1, glucose 3.1 just after delivery → Cut insulin: placenta gone

f: Diabetic ketoacidosis

Occurs at lower glucose in pregnancy · Ketones, pH below 7.3, HCO₃⁻ below 15 · Saline 1 L in the first hour, insulin 0.1 U/kg/h, dextrose once glucose below 14, K⁺ once below 5.5 · Fetal distress: treat the mother first, not an emergency CS
